reasoning: The bright interdendritic phase appears as a continuous network in (a), as isolated particles in (b), and as thin broken strings in (c), showing that RE addition turns the continuous coarse netlike interdendritic phase into discontinuous, finer particles, with La refining it more than Sm [obs1][s1].

Extra reflections at roughly 21-37, 50, and 67 degrees appear only in the Al-Cu-Mn-La diffraction pattern while the Sm pattern matches the RE-free one, showing that La forms a new Al6Cu6La phase of cubic NaZn13 type at dendrite boundaries while Sm forms no new phase [obs2][s2].
Arrow B in (c) marks a second, finer bright boundary phase beside the arrow-A particles, consistent with this distinct La-associated phase sitting alongside the coarser boundary particles [obs3][s2].

The La alloy shows a weak peak A near 605 C and a shoulder B near 638 C, assigned to dissolution of Al2Cu and of the Al6Cu6La phase respectively, corroborating that La introduces this new phase with its own dissolution signature [obs4][s2].

Precipitate plate lengths of about 20-40 nm in (a), about 10 nm in (b), and about 5-10 nm in (c) show that RE addition refines the theta' platelets on {001}Al, with La refining them more than Sm [obs5][s5].
Precipitate number density visibly rises from (a) to (b) to (c), showing that RE addition raises the number density of theta' precipitates, with La raising it more than Sm [obs6][s6].

Taking the distribution, the new phase identity, and the feature sizes from step 1 as given, the same rise in precipitate number density from (a) to (b) to (c) is used in step 2 to again establish that RE addition raises theta' precipitate number density, with La more than Sm [obs1][s6].
